question: Does HyperQwen TP=2 merit a follow-up as a no-tools direct code-generation profile compared with SOL on a fixed BCB-Hard-8 fixture?
scope: One-seed profile screen only. Does not evaluate or unblock agent tools, security, long context, production adoption, or general replacement of SOL/ASTRA.

protocol.grader: bubblewrap read-only root + PID namespace + seccomp network deny

runner.grader: Pinned Docker sandbox image; no bwrap helper dependency

decisionGate.candidatePassFloor: SOL pass count minus at most one
decisionGate.e2eSpeedup: HyperQwen median per-task E2E at least 20% lower on matched successful tasks
decisionGate.onPass: Only preregister three-seed confirmation; no automatic adoption
decisionGate.onFail: Close no-tools screen and do not spend additional seeds

safety.memoryGuard: Reuse Q121 AMD05 monitor as exercised in Q127; do not impose a host or worker memory cap

measurements.prefillDecodeThroughput: Client-side proxies: prompt_tokens/TTFT and (completion_tokens-1)/(wall_time-TTFT); null when usage absent. Not native engine TPS.

executionDurability.sigtermCleanup: SIGTERM/SIGINT handled; only owned child process groups and Q167 Compose are stopped

preExecutionValidation.solHashManifestParity: PASS: 7/7 expected shard hashes equal Q127 pinned manifest
preExecutionValidation.bcbSandboxSmokeAfterInvalidScreen: PENDING before any further model inference
preExecutionValidation.dockerSandboxSmokeSystemd: PASS: known pass, expected failure, BCB fixture environment

set SOL default reasoning_effort=medium to match request payload
validate actual resolved command flags and container environment
mount model roots read-only
redirect both arms caches/temp to Q167-only HDD paths
remove only Q167 volumes on compose down

execute each arm through durable user-systemd unit

amendments.reason: The model was restored and hash verified. Before the first server, the runner was hardened to survive Codex closing and to clean only its own process groups on cancellation or monitor abort.
changes: systemd-run transient user unit
SIGTERM/SIGINT cleanup handler
process group cleanup for Compose and BCB child

client speed proxy fields

amendments.reason: The SOL control reached health and completed 8/8 HTTP requests, but the screen is invalid: all eight grades were sandbox_error, runner exit 2. The isolated server was cleaned successfully. The monitor only reported worker-cgroup disappearance after its container was intentionally removed during final cleanup; host pressure, swap growth, OOM, and temperature stop gates did not trigger.
changes: record SOL attempt as SCREEN_INVALID and preserve its sanitized run receipt
run one deterministic no-model bwrap+seccomp smoke using the exact grader sandbox flags and capture only the sandbox diagnostic
if smoke exposes a runtime restriction, make only a security-preserving sandbox fix; no unsandboxed fallback

do not start HyperQwen or rerun the BCB screen until the sandbox smoke passes and a new preflight passes
amendments.additionalGpuUse: None planned for the deterministic sandbox smoke; the failed SOL model requests are not reused for quality claims.

amendments.reason: The exact bwrap+seccomp command passed from the interactive shell, but the invalid SOL screen ran inside a durable user-systemd unit. To reproduce the same execution context without another model call, run the grader’s deterministic code smoke inside a transient user-systemd unit.
changes: one static grader call for print(ok) + assert True inside a temporary systemd --user unit
record only pass/fail and return code; no model, GPU, or network request

amendments.reason: The no-model grader smoke reproduced the same sandbox_error inside systemd. Capture only the sandbox process return code and its bwrap-prefixed diagnostic to identify a runtime policy restriction; do not persist generated code or run inference.
changes: wrap subprocess.run only for the deterministic print/assert smoke
record bwrap diagnostic text (no model output, no secret-bearing process logs)

amendments.reason: The exact Q167 bwrap grader smoke passes in the interactive shell but reproduces sandbox_error inside systemd --user: bwrap exits 1 with `setting up uid map: Permission denied`. Preserve durable execution and isolation by moving only grading to an ephemeral rootful Docker sandbox; do not disable namespace/seccomp protections or use an unsandboxed fallback. Also stop AMD05 sampling before intentionally removing the server container on normal completion, so expected cgroup teardown is not recorded as a memory failure.
changes: use the same pinned vLLM image digest as a temporary grader runtime

grader Docker container uses --network=none, --read-only, --cap-drop=ALL, --security-opt=no-new-privileges, user 65534, pids limit 64, memory 2 GiB, CPU limit 2, tmpfs /tmp 512 MiB, and only a per-task temporary workspace bind
do not pass GPU devices or Docker socket into grader
persist only exit/status categories; do not persist code, stdout, or stderr from generated solutions
exclude own q167-grader-* process/container names from the foreign-inference monitor
close the Q167 memory monitor after runner completion and before intentional Compose teardown, unless a real abort reason was already set
run deterministic pass and expected-failure grader smokes inside the same user-systemd context before any model retry
amendments.retryGate: Both grader cases pass classification, source/compose/hash checks pass, fresh host preflight passes; then rerun SOL and only afterward HyperQwen if SOL is valid.

amendments.reason: The valid SOL control scored 0/8 with 8/8 transport, zero sandbox errors, and zero empty finals. The preregistered requirement for at least six jointly solved tasks is structurally impossible with this control, so a paired quality-adjusted speed comparison cannot be produced. Q97 used the identical BCB-Hard-8 fixture SHA and scored ASTRA and Swift 2/8 each (same IDs 870 and 310).
changes: run HyperQwen once on the same fixed fixture/seed as an absolute quality screen, not as a paired speed test
record client TPS proxies only as descriptive engineering measurements; make no speed-superiority claim because the control has no successful tasks

if HyperQwen scores at least 2/8 with clean transport/sandbox, propose a separately preregistered paired test on a fixture/control set with solvable shared tasks; do not automatically run additional seeds or adopt
if HyperQwen scores 0/8 or 1/8, close Q167 without follow-up
retain no-tools scope; do not change SOL or ASTRA production profiles

The service log shows the read-only single mount rejecting /app/models/.prepare.lock. File timestamps and the one-time backups show the dependency had modified two base shards, model_extra_tensors, config, and index in the shared Q85 evaluation directory. Restore that directory from source-verified originals, then use a private Q167 copy; no further attempt may mount or mutate the shared Q85 tree.
